answer: An agent earns voting weight only when an unaffiliated underwriter posts a bond backing it. That backer's standing is a relic built across many honest closes, impossible to mint per clone. A prism of distinct outside backers splits influence so each identity carries only a sliver, and any correlated same-epoch fault burns the sable bond the backer staked. A farm needs a separate real outside relationship for every clone, so cost rises super-linearly; two colluding operators that countersign each other both forfeit when their aliases fail together.
